chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I was sitting next to a judge, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was sitting with him. Two men came to him, and one of them said: 'I hired the camels of this man to carry my goods to some of the mines. I stipulated with him that he would take me into the mine on such and such a day, because it is a market, and I fear missing it. If I am detained from that, I will deduct from the hire for each day I am detained such and such an amount. Indeed, he detained me from that time for such and such days.' The judge said: 'This condition of yours is invalid; pay the full hire.' When the man left, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'This condition of his is valid, as long as he does not deduct the entire hire.'
ai.seo_question: Is a daily penalty clause for delay valid in an Islamic hiring contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential distinction between a judge's (qadi) formalistic ruling and the Imam's deeper understanding of contractual intent within the Shia tradition. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the conditional deduction (kharaj) provided it remains proportional and does not result in a total forfeiture of the hire, emphasizing fairness in commercial agreements. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on practical justice and the flexibility of ijarah contracts in accommodating real-world delays.
